links.outcome: Patient-rated readability, comprehension, and language of AI vs human translation
links.effect: Before face validation, ChatGPT-4 translation scored median 4 vs 5 for human on readability (p=0.008), understandability (p=0.004), appropriate language (p=0.001), overall (p=0.002); 90% preferred human version.
links.quote: Before face validation, the human-translated version of the questionnaire was rated at least one point higher on the parameters of readability, comprehension, appropriate use of language, and overall opinion of the questionnaire (Table 2 ).

links.outcome: Translation quality ratings after face validation with patient end users and revision
links.effect: After face validation, no significant differences: readability p=0.341, understandability p=0.082, appropriate language p=0.359, overall p=0.100; preference for human fell from 90% to 50%.
links.quote: After face validation, there were no significant differences regarding readability, comprehension, appropriate use of language, and overall opinion of the questionnaire (Table 2 ).

openai.sample_unit: patients assessing both translations before face validation; 18 also assessed them afterward

links.outcome: Patient-rated comprehension before and after patient face validation and questionnaire revision
links.effect: ChatGPT-4 understandability increased from 4 (2–5) to 5 (3–5); human medians remained 5. Between-translation p-values were 0.004 before and 0.082 after face validation. Results were not stratified by literacy.
links.quote: While the human-translated questionnaire initially performed better in terms of readability, comprehension, and appropriate use of language, the differences between the two versions disappeared following face validation.

links.outcome: Patient-rated readability of AI-translated versus human-translated questionnaires
links.effect: Before face validation, readability was 4 (3–5) for ChatGPT-4 versus 5 (4–5) for humans, p=0.008; afterward, both were 5 (3–5), p=0.341.
links.quote: After face validation, there were no significant differences in the measured parameters, and half of the participants preferred the version translated by humans, whereas before face validation, the human-translated questionnaire outperformed the version translated by ChatGPT-4 in all parameters and was preferred by almost all participants.

links.effect: Comparing AI to human translation revealed ChatGPT-4 scored significantly lower on readability, understandability, and appropriate language before face validation.
links.quote: Before face validation, the human-translated version of the questionnaire was rated at least one point higher on the parameters of readability, comprehension, appropriate use of language, and overall opinion of the questionnaire

links.effect: Conducting face validation with representative patients allowed correction of the AI's shortcomings, eliminating significant differences in understandability compared to human translation.
links.quote: However, the lack of significant differences after face validation implies that ChatGPT-4’s shortcomings were corrected through the face validation process.
